abstract: While unified audio generators can synthesize speech, music, and sound effects within a single model, producing a plausible mixture is only part of the challenge: a complex scene request also specifies which events occur, who produces them, and when they are heard. To satisfy these compositional constraints in a single generation pass, we present SonicRender, a unified multi-event audio renderer. Its Temporal Audio Scene Graph (TASG) binds persistent source identities to localized speech, music, ambience, and sound-effect events, together with their content, acoustic roles, relations, and timestamped windows. We further introduce AbsTime, which supplies the audio latent stream with absolute-frame coordinates and valid-canvas duration. Through joint text-audio attention and conditional flow matching, the renderer learns to realize structured, timed scenes as coherent mixtures. On the MMAG timestamp benchmark, SonicRender achieves speech/sound F1 scores of 0.79/0.60, exceeding the strongest reported scores in our comparison. On our SceneMix evaluation, it attains 85.4% all-event recall, 83.9% window-hit rate, and 95.7% speaker accuracy. Subjective study further demonstrates significant improvements over all five comparison systems in both perceived audio quality and scene realization. Results across speech, general audio, music, multi-event load, and temporal-grounding analyses establish precise, composition-aware audio rendering within a unified generator. Demo page: https://caiyunrui.github.io/SonicRender.

oneSentenceThesis: 针对单次生成中漏事件、错说话人与放错时间的问题，SonicRender 以 TASG 绑定身份与事件并以 AbsTime 把秒级窗口落到潜在帧，在 SceneMix 取得 85.4% 事件召回与 83.9% 窗口命中且听测显著领先，代价是依赖整数秒时钟与内部大规模数据及模型裁判。
originalTitle: SonicRender: Structured and Time-Grounded Rendering of Multi-Event Audio Scene Generation
readerTitle: 结构化时间接地实现多事件音频场景的一次渲染
